claims.text: US President Donald Trump stated on Friday, October 2, that the United States would not impose a diesel export ban.
Donald Trump praised European countries for agreeing to release fuel from their strategic reserves.
Donald Trump first expressed support for a US diesel export ban on September 22.
G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from their reserves over four months.
G7 member countries agreed in a joint statement to refrain from imposing energy export restrictions on one another.
French President Emmanuel Macron stated the G7 agreed to release reserves of 'up to 100 million barrels' within four months under International Energy Agency coordination.
The price of global benchmark Brent crude oil briefly fell below $100 a barrel before rising back to around $102 on Friday evening.
Prior to the US and Israel invading Iran, Brent crude oil was trading at approximately $73 a barrel.
US domestic refineries produce about four to five million barrels of diesel daily, with domestic consumption at roughly 3.6 million barrels per day.
Russia implemented an export ban on diesel after attacks on its refineries by Ukrainian forces.
US President Donald Trump posted on social media that Europe agreed to release a 'massive amount' of diesel from emergency stockpiles.
Under proposals formulated by French President Emmanuel Macron, G7 members will release 50 million barrels of diesel and 50 million barrels of crude oil.
US diesel pump prices rose above $5.85 a gallon for the first time in early September.
Average diesel prices at UK pumps reached a record high of £2 per litre on Friday.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez reported that 1,747 people were arrested on Friday during widespread student protests.
French Justice Minister Gérard Darmanin stated that 735 out of France's 3,700 schools were affected by violent demonstrations.
French Education Minister Édouard Geffray stated that the student protest movement had been hijacked by individuals who were not students.
A 17-year-old was arrested in Belfort, north-eastern France, on suspicion of attempted homicide following an attack on a police officer.
At least 65 education staff members were injured during the student unrest in France.
The regional government reported that Nelson Mandela high school in Nantes suffered more than €2 million in damage due to fire.
The French Ministry of National Education stated that 564 schools were affected on Friday and nearly 400 high schools were expected to stay closed.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray stated that more than 1,200 high schools have experienced disruptions or blockades during the protests.
French authorities reported more than 1,900 arrests and 305 police officer injuries on Thursday.
Fires damaged the entrances of Léonard de Vinci high school and Gaston-Bachelard high school in Paris on Friday morning.
The French Education Ministry reported that 65 education staff members were injured, including 40 school principals.
Roughly 400 secondary schools across France were closed on Friday, October 2.
According to Le Monde, over 1,020 schools were affected by strikes or protests on Thursday, including 222 blockades.
Spain's parliament narrowly voted down two emergency government decrees intended to address rising rental housing costs.
The first emergency housing decree was rejected by a vote of 178 to 172 in the Chamber of Deputies.
The second emergency decree failed in Spain's parliament by a vote of 184 to 166.
Protests across Spain were triggered by the eviction of 87-year-old Madrid resident Maricarmen Abascal from her apartment.
Housing rents in Spain have approximately doubled over the past decade.
The conservative People's Party, far-right Vox, and Catalan pro-independence party Junts joined together to vote against both housing decrees.
According to the Youth Council of Spain, average rent in Spain rose to €1,176 per month, representing 98.7% of the average salary for under-30s.
A protest encampment in Madrid's Puerta del Sol plaza expanded to include more than 1,200 tents.
The Spanish Tenants' Union (Sindicato de Inquilinas) announced it was ending its tent protest in central Madrid to focus organization efforts on local neighborhoods.
Maricarmen Abascal was evicted after being unable to pay a rent increase imposed by real estate company Urbagestión.
Maricarmen Abascal was evicted on September 23 from her Madrid apartment, where she had lived for about seven decades.
The United States suspended consular services in Brazil on Friday due to security concerns ahead of Sunday's presidential election.
Australia closed its embassy in Brasilia on Friday in response to the US security alert.
Brazil's federal police conducted search warrants in Sao Paulo and the Federal District regarding potential threats to US facilities but found no corroborating evidence.
Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting a coup.
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva led a large campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro ahead of the presidential election.
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva told the Flow podcast that he decided to run for a fourth term because he believes only he can prevent Flávio Bolsonaro's family from returning to power.
Flávio Bolsonaro announced plans to appoint five conservative judges to Brazil's supreme court if elected president.
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced his candidacy for a fourth presidential term in August 2026.
Lula launched his 2026 presidential re-election campaign at a stadium in Sao Bernardo do Campo, Sao Paulo.
Ethiopia and Eritrea severed diplomatic relations as fighting intensified in northern Ethiopia.
The Ethiopian military advanced toward the Tigrayan regional capital of Mekelle.
Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara and ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave the country within 48 hours.
A pro-government militia stated it seized the town of Milazat, located 20 kilometers southeast of Mekelle.
Explosions were heard overnight near Ethiopia's military headquarters in the capital, Addis Ababa.
Ethiopia expelled an Egyptian diplomat, prompting Egypt to reciprocate by ordering an Ethiopian embassy official to leave.
An African Union mediator previously estimated that around 600,000 people died during the 2020-2022 Tigray war.
A doctor in Alamata stated that at least 52 civilians were killed during three days of intense fighting.
The 2022 Pretoria Peace Agreement officially ended two years of conflict between Ethiopia's federal government and the TPLF.

An opposition coalition formed against the Ethiopian federal government includes the TPLF, Oromo Liberation Army, a faction of the Ogaden National Liberation Front, Afar militant groups, and Benishangul-Gumuz factions.
A woman accusing men of gang rape at Cornell University told disciplinary investigators she 'felt like bait' during an October 2024 encounter at the Chi Phi fraternity house.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul appointed State Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to reopen the Cornell gang rape criminal investigation.
Cornell University's Title IX disciplinary investigation involved 50 interviews with 32 witnesses and 12 days of hearings.
Attorney Thomas Giuffra stated his client Jane Doe was 'under siege' on social media from users attempting to identify her.
An active-duty US Marine Corps sergeant sharing the name of one accused student was incorrectly served with Jane Doe's lawsuit.
Governor Kathy Hochul signed an executive order directing Attorney General Letitia James to investigate the Cornell sexual assault allegations.
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten declined to prosecute the Cornell case in November 2024 based on a six-page police statement.
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten reopened his investigation after Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against seven Chi Phi fraternity members.
Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike survived an execution attempt involving two doses of pentobarbital and remains in critical condition.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused all executions for the remainder of his term following Christa Pike's failed execution.
The family of Renee Good filed two civil lawsuits against the federal government over her fatal shooting by an ICE agent in Minnesota.
